hypothesis: The TWI11, USB2, radio and CE parent-admission functions accept a normalized 24 MHz reference on 24, 26 and 19.2 MHz boards and reject invalid factors.
conclusion: Configured-rate admission passed on the host for the four providers; board frequencies and operation were not measured.
narrative: checks/provider-clock-reference.py (removed from the repository as waived pending re-qualification against the current board image) compiled the actual changed clock-check function bodies against the actual public structures with address and undefined-behavior sanitizers. TWI used the complete native prepare function; USB2, radio and CE used their parent-admission functions. The check accepted valid 24, 26 and 19.2 MHz normalization, rejected invalid factors and lost enable/lock state, covered the selected TWI and radio PERI0 paths, and preserved CE's separate TRNG RC16M requirement. Register reads and existing lock, pin, time and ownership dependencies were modeled. It was not a whole-provider or native-startup execution. Evidence directory provider-clock-reference-20261020 retained fixture setup repairs and previously completed cases; only affected or unexecuted cases resumed. A focused source review found no remaining parent/rate mismatch. No application image was rebuilt. The source checks establish configured-rate admission, not measured board frequencies, electrical readiness, radio operation, USB transfers, camera operation or CE execution.

hypothesis: The I2S AUDIO1 reference and PWM profile guards accept normalized references and refuse raw-24 MHz-only routes on a 26 MHz board.
conclusion: The I2S and PWM guards behave as designed on the host; no board run.
narrative: The cases were selected without replaying the earlier four providers, with `checks/provider-clock-reference.py --providers i2s pwm --output evidence`. Both providers passed with address and undefined-behavior sanitizers against the actual reference() and profile() function bodies and public structures. The cases covered valid oscillator encodings, malformed reference/enable state, PWM PERI0 rate mismatch, LED source-0 refusal at 26 and 19.2 MHz, source-4 acceptance and APBS0 readback mismatch. A delta source review found no remaining mismatch. Earlier provider evidence remained under its original frozen inputs. No HDMI, whole-image, startup or physical checks were executed.

hypothesis: The native HDMI TV0 pattern path prepares, starts and stops the 720p pattern on modeled raw 26 MHz hardware while retaining REF and the other resources.

conditions.model: raw 26 MHz oscillator, modeled architectural services, scheduling, MMIO, electrical state and analog admission

conclusion: The native 720p path admits raw 26 MHz and refuses the three unsafe cases on the host model. No electrical or standard-compliance qualification is claimed for either nominal mode or the approximate raw-26 MHz clocks.
narrative: checks/hdmi-clock-native.py (removed from the repository as a waived image-bound check) built the native TV0 pattern target once and reused its compiled provider, controller, PHY and ownership objects in a focused composition. On modeled raw 26 MHz hardware the actual native path prepared, started and stopped the 720p pattern while retaining REF and the other resources. The native requests and the supplied record named the same raw reference. Separate continuations from the saved baseline refused raw 19.2 MHz, a missing REF lock, and an observed raw rate that differed from the admitted request, all before VO1 or local HDMI writes. The executed trace matched the pinned 26 MHz TOP row, internal PHY words and color conversion. The source audit retained DDC's normalized 24 MHz timing basis. The calculated 720p pixel rate is 73.9375 MHz; source-row and host-profile checks also covered the 147.875 MHz 1080p plan, which was not executed in this native case. The 24 MHz protocol and reference evidence remained under its original frozen inputs. manifest.json bound the image, composition, sources, artifacts, CPU/RAM checkpoints and results. The initial nominal case completed before a postprocessing checkpoint-label error; the corrected check verified saved executable bytes and resumed only the unfinished comparison and refusal cases without rebuilding or repeating the nominal path. Firmware boot, GIC/startup and physical HDMI operation were not executed.
